page: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Faldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, the processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core.

This server includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the F16alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core metrics, and single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores remain strong. The local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage, making it suitable for disk-bound operations.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 1:2, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The combination of high single-core clock speeds and fast local NVMe storage makes it well-suited for tasks such as image processing, text processing, software compilation, and lightweight LLM inference. It is also appropriate for web serving and database operations that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and fast local storage.
